edges.dependent: MPLS Traffic Engineering and Fast Restoration
edges.rationale: Traffic engineering and fast reroute are built on MPLS's label-switching mechanism: explicit paths and precomputed failover paths are implemented as label-switched paths, so understanding labels, LSRs, and FECs is required first.

edges.prerequisite: Data Center Purposes and Traffic Types
edges.rationale: The hierarchical architecture (tiers, TOR switches, redundancy, VLAN partitioning) is motivated by the need to support external client-to-host and internal host-to-host traffic; understanding the purposes and traffic types explains why the design takes this shape.

Multipath routing (ECMP, flow-level load balancing, packet splitting) exploits the rich inter-tier connectivity and redundancy of the hierarchical data center topology; without knowing the architecture, the multipath designs make no sense.
